neighbours.label: competitive application or selection: the link from a candidate to the post, place or prize sought (applied to, shortlisted for, admitted into, tenders for)
fire: More than two hundred candidates applied for the three vacancies in the fire service.
Her nephew was accepted into the conservatoire on his second attempt.
The novel was nominated for the Prix Goncourt but lost to a debut from Marseille.
Each spring thousands of teenagers compete for a handful of places at the academy.
He put himself forward for the vacant seat on the parish council.
Only one in twelve applicants is admitted to the veterinary school in Utrecht.
She interviewed for a junior post at the embassy and heard nothing for weeks.
Three firms submitted tenders for the contract to rebuild the harbour wall.
quiet: More than two hundred firefighters responded to the blaze at the warehouse.
Her nephew walked into the conservatoire to collect his lost umbrella.
The novel was translated into French by a teacher from Marseille.
Each spring thousands of teenagers travel to the coast for the holidays.
He sat down in the vacant seat at the back of the parish hall.
Only one in twelve dogs treated at the veterinary school in Utrecht needs surgery.
She wrote to the embassy about her lost passport and heard nothing for weeks.
Three firms delivered stone for the rebuilding of the harbour wall.

notes: Card peaks are ' to'/' for'/' into' after applying, selection, admission, hopeful, application. The + pole peaks on 'candidates'/'applicant'. Near misses keep the verbs and the institutions but remove the candidacy (walked into the conservatoire, responded to the blaze, delivered stone for the rebuilding).
